gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga spaces its flat, uniform strokes generously. Stencilia, a striking display face with gaps cut into its curves, feels structural beside that plain sans, like a stamped frame around open, easy lines.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend-mega: Gaps cut into the curve ends give Stencilia its stenciled, structural look. And Lexend Mega follows in a sans-serif drawn with one nib, approachable and modern, so the heading's sharp cuts sit against smooth, gap-mouthed letters.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend-peta: Striking and structural, Stencilia leads with its stencil-cut curves and a compact line height. Lexend Peta handles the quieter job, a wire-like line with wide-mouthed c shapes and a big x-height that keeps the text approachable.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend-tera: Stencilia is a display face with spacious gaps at its curve terminals, and it feels striking and structural. But Lexend Tera is the real surprise, a plotter-pen line with stepping-stone spacing that makes the pair feel contemporary.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta runs wide, with ribbon-like strokes and tall small letters. Over a long passage it feels approachable and contemporary, an unhurried line of simple, one-tip shapes under Stencilia's structural, gap-cut display heading.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-montserrat-alter: Stencilia, a striking display face, opens its curve terminals wide and tucks the gap between its x-height and ascender line tight. Montserrat Alternates reads steadily, its round letters crowding toward the capital line.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code reads with a modern, wire-like monoline stroke and a lot of space between neighbors. But if Stentiga, the refined, spread-out display heading, were made small, its luxurious tracking would lose its drama.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-cascadia-mono: Stentiga looks refined, with tracking opened up wide. Cascadia Mono sits beneath it like pins in a board, a plain sans whose curves match its stems and whose capitals blend into the lowercase.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-julius-sans-one: Light, luxurious, spread out. Stentiga stretches its letters with generous tracking, and Julius Sans One follows in a plain sans where capitals and lowercase nearly match, so paragraphs feel open and approachable.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads as a plain sans with a big x-height, stubby ascenders and wide-open curves that stay distinct. And across a long passage it feels professional and clean, a steady counterpart to Stentiga's refined, luxurious display heading.
